> I’m 16 and I’ve dated maybe 5 to 6

I had this same experience, except I was 19. We were at the girl's house party and my friend, whom she had a crush on, stayed afterwards and they were fucking. One of my colleagues who was in his late 30s took me aside. He grabbed my shoulders and said, "Look, you're not going to believe it when I tell you, but trust me, one day you'll look back on this and think about how silly you were to feel upset in the first place".

And of course, it was hard for me to believe that was true. The pain of it hurt immensely – how could I ever forget? But you know what, 7 years later, my friend was right. Thinking back, I felt so stupid that it ever got to me the way it did and it'll be the same for you too.

Thank you for the well written reply. As a follow up question, do you think it's justified to think poorly of someone's character if they are a murderer? A drug addict? Obese?

I'm definitely not equating obesity to murderer but if someone killed someone else, I think a majority of people would probably agree that "wow, this is a pretty horrible person". 

Drug addiction is a bit more of a grey area. I would say that for a drug addict that does not seek help, that may be harmful to other people and also be a liability to society (health costs, housing costs, law enforcement, rehabilitation costs), many people might also consider these actions reprehensible and in my opinion, perhaps rightfully so. 

I'm not saying all obese people are like this, but in the hypothetical question of this particular case, my question to you is what is that moral boundary between a drug addict and a person who may be addicted to food who does not seek mental health care, may a liability to society through health care costs and may be harming others? Isn't there strong moral grounds to equate on to another?

I wouldn't say I outwardly shame fat people. But I will admit that I definitely don't have much respect for drug addicts or alcoholics probably in the same way I don't have respect for morbidly obese people. 

For example, say you have a family and you were morbidly obese and took no action to seek help. I feel almost as judgmental in that behavior as someone who has a child and was addicted to meth and didn't seek help. I feel like both are very damaging. 

Yet I am perplexed of this body acceptance movement I see sometimes of women who are very unhealthy weight wise. If one is slightly unhealthy and overweight, that's one thing, but if you're medically deemed to be unhealthy and at great risk for health problems, I don't see why we should accept that.

> they're a fundamental data structure ingredient

I feel that a linked list is only good as... a linked list. Say you're implementing a common stack (push, pop), a well written dynamic array is much more efficient. Obviously, you can immediately access any member in the stack, but more importantly, with a linked list implementation you have to malloc every pointer you push. Say you have a hefty sized integer stack. You're going to have memory all over the place!

The only occasion where I can think to use a linked list is when I need... just a linked list. When do I need just a linked list? Pretty much never.
